chapter: Clarinetists, brass bands and the day job
title: Big Eye Louis and the C versus B flat clarinet
summary: Big Eye played C clarinet most of his life and mastered it better than B flat, though local players mostly used B flat and E flat.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Yeah. He just started playing the B flat in the late years, around in the Friday like that. Yeah, he used to play C clarinet, Big Illo. That's how Piku played with me, because Piku was playing alto. And the clarinet and I was playing clarinet soprano.
Did Big I sound much different on the C than he did on the B flat? Was there much difference?
He could master the C better than the B flat.
He thought he was better on that.
Yeah, he could master the C better. Naturally, he was brought up on the C.
From a boy to the man, he was aged when he was over eight or ten years on the B when he died. But he was from a boy up to a man in his fifties.
Why did he change, you think, August?

Well, you see, they wasn't using very much C's around here. They wasn't using very much C's. The only clarinet they were using around here was the B flat. Now, some fellows used to carry A flat for transposition. But they just used to use the B flat and do the same transposition on that B flat. Well, I guess Big I must have- You see, it was much easier for transposition if you had- Some fellows used to carry three, four clarinets. The A, the B, the D, and what's the other one, the E scale?
The little short one is the E flat.

E flat. Yeah, E flat. The little short one, E flat. They scale all the instruments. See, they used the E flat mostly in the brass band. They would use the E flat. But I never used but one. I never used but one.
